Alex: Quick sync — we keep seeing a single tenant hog large backfill slices and pushing low-priority replays to the tail. want to discuss a lightweight heuristic to improve fairness without huge scheduling changes. :thinking:
Maya: Yep saw that in the dashboard yesterday. one tenant's spike consumed ~60% of concurrent slots for 2h.
Jamal: Is this the same case where the tenant also had a huge backlog age? I remember a long-running ingest delay.
Alex: Not always. sometimes it's fresh but very wide (many small partitions) so they win many slices concurrently.
Maya: Proposal: introduce a per-tenant short-term consumption metric and apply a temporary fairness_boost that reduces weight for tenants over a threshold. keep it local to the backfill scheduler so we don't touch the quota service yet.
Rachel: From Console UX point — if we add fairness, show an explicit "fairness applied" badge per slice and a little graph of recent slot consumption so SREs can see why their job slowed. don't hide it. :eyes:
Jamal: Agree on visual transparency. for the heuristic itself, we'd want something like: lower priority tenants get a multiplicative boost if their mean completed slices is below median. not deterministic slot steal, just soft weighting.
Alex: Draft pseudocode I sketched locally: 
```
# backfill slice weight heuristic (pseudo)
base_priority = tenant_priority_rank  # 0=low,1=mid,2=high
backlog_hours = min(72, hours_oldest_event)
recent_consumption = tenant_slots_last_30m / median_slots_last_30m
fairness_boost = 0.0
if recent_consumption > 1.5:
    fairness_boost = -0.25  # reduce weight for hogs
elif recent_consumption < 0.5:
    fairness_boost = 0.15   # favor under-served tenants
weight = (1 + fairness_boost) * (1 + backlog_hours/48) * (1 + base_priority*0.2)
# scheduler orders slices by descending weight
```
Maya: I like keeping parameters conservative (-25% to +15%) so we dont thrash. also add a decay window so a tenant recovers after consumption returns to baseline.
Jamal: Important: avoid starvation for high-priority SLA tenants. ensure a floor for high priority: weight_high >= 0.8 even if fairness_boost negative.
Alex: Good call. also think about implementing this as a duck-typed plugin: scheduler checks for `weight_adjustment(tenant_id)` and applies it. That keeps fallback easy.
Rachel: On Console: suggestion to add a "why" tooltip when fairness triggers that points to the metric (recent_slots / median_slots). Should be a one-liner not a wall of logs.
Maya: Operational question — do we need to persist per-tenant recent_consumption in Redis or can we compute from existing slot metrics? computing on the fly from metrics (prometheus) might be enough with a cache.
Jamal: If we rely on prometheus queries per-slice decision, that will be slow. better to maintain a small in-memory LRU cache in the scheduler with periodic rollup from metrics every 30s.
Alex: Agreed — store ephemeral counters in scheduler process and fall back to median defaults if missing. avoids touching quota DB.
infra-bot: scheduled job created: `backfill-fairness-experiment-v1` will run on canary cluster at 11:00 UTC tomorrow for 3h.
Maya: Experiment plan: enable heuristic on canary, cap scope to tenants with >1000 slices queued, and monitor: average tail latency, slot utilization, per-tenant throughput, and Console fairness flag counts.
Jamal: Add an alert: if any high-priority tenant sees >20% throughput degradation vs baseline for 10m, auto-disable heuristic.
Rachel: I'll add the Console flag visuals and a small panel showing the recent_consumption metric per tenant. will mock in Figma and send link.
Alex: For rollout, can we gate via feature flag + config weights? so we can tune fairness_boost and decay windows without redeploy.
Maya: yes, config-driven. I'll add keys: `fairness_enabled`, `fairness_boost_thresholds`, `decay_window_sec`, `min_high_priority_floor`.
Jamal: One more thought — we should run the heuristic on historical traces offline to verify it doesn't cause regressions in historical jobs. a replay with our replayer for last 30 days.
Alex: Good call — run replayer sim with canary settings and compare per-tenant completion times.
Maya: I'll kick off a dry run today and attach results in this thread.
Alex: Thanks all. next steps: Maya runs dry-run and posts numbers, Rachel posts Console mock, Jamal wires the safety alert. we'll re-evaluate after canary window. :thumbsup:
